title: The Protocol of Kowloon
premise: Orsen Galloway, a crash investigator whose spouse and daughter died in row twelve of Flight 4471, has spent five years buried in procedure—until a routine voiceprint authentication unlocks a server in Lagos that shouldn't know their name. The server belongs to Meridian, the private network that trained Orsen as an investigator and quietly engineered the crash that killed their family, and it has been waiting for them to come looking. Hunted by the handlers who made them and tethered to Nia Adeyemi, a Meridian defector whose loyalty keeps colliding with her orders, Orsen traces the network's roots across three continents while learning their own memories were partly installed. At the Geneva aviation summit, where Meridian plans to embed its protocol into global air-traffic law, Orsen chooses love over duty for the first time, exposes the training archive publicly, and burns the servers—but only by surrendering the last fabricated memory of their daughter, ending the book invisible at last, and finally free.
about_author: T. M. Kavanagh is the pen name of a former aviation-safety analyst who spent a decade writing incident reports before turning to fiction. They live near a regional airport and still flinch at takeoff announcements.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Five years after the crash, Orsen works a routine runway incident in Manchester, reciting protocol like prayer. A flashback to identifying their family's belongings establishes grief-as-procedure. Emotional beat: numb competence cracking when a passenger asks if anyone ever really reads the reports.

chapters.title: The Voice That Answers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Submitting a standard records request, Orsen's voiceprint unexpectedly authenticates against an encrypted server in Lagos flagged MERIDIAN-7. The system greets them by a childhood nickname no living person should know. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Nia
chapters.summary: Nia Adeyemi's POV. In Lagos, Meridian analyst Nia is ordered to monitor the intruder she realizes is a designed asset, not a hacker. She stalls her handlers, buying Orsen hours. Beat: first flicker of conscience—and attraction—to someone she's meant to surveil.

chapters.title: Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Back home, Orsen finds their five-year-old investigation files altered: dates shifted, a witness deleted. Their supervisor gently suggests leave. Beat: gaslit paranoia; the rules were never neutral.

chapters.title: What the Training Made
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Orsen flies to Lagos off-book; Nia intercepts them at the airport, torn between her extraction order and warning them. She shows them one file: Orsen's own recruitment assessment, dated two years before they remember applying. Beat: identity begins to unmoor.

chapters.title: The Archive of Orsen Galloway
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Inside a Meridian safehouse, Orsen reads their own life like a syllabus—grief engineered into reliability, row twelve possibly selected. They find a second name on the file: Nia's, marked 'handler-track.' Beat: betrayal and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Run, Investigator
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Meridian activates a cleanup team. Nia burns her own clearance to get Orsen out of Lagos, choosing defection mid-act. Beat: duty inverted; love chosen before it's admitted.

chapters.title: Lisbon Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The pair regroup in Lisbon with a defector archivist, Tomas, who explains Meridian's endgame: embedding its behavioral protocol into ICAO standards at the Geneva summit in six weeks. Beat: the mission acquires a clock.

chapters.title: Installed Memories
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Under Tomas's neural-archive reader, Orsen learns which memories are real—and that their most comforting memory of their daughter, a beach morning, was inserted post-crash to stabilize them. Beat: devastation; grief must be re-grieved from scratch.

chapters.title: The Handler's Call
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Director Voss, who trained Orsen personally, offers amnesty: return, forget, be restored. He genuinely believes he saved Orsen. Beat: the villain as loving parent; temptation made reasonable.

chapters.title: Nia's Ledger
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Nia confesses she wrote parts of Orsen's training curriculum—her voice is the one in their de-escalation drills. Orsen's fury nearly ends the alliance. Beat: love against duty becomes love despite complicity.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Interlude
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Chased through Frankfurt by cleanup operatives, Orsen uses their own trained protocols to anticipate the hunters—the training turned against its makers. First kill or near-kill. Beat: competence as horror.

chapters.title: Tomas's Price
chapters.summary: Tomas POV chapter. The archivist reveals the burn requires biometric keys from three founders—one dead, one in Geneva, one missing. His price for help: his daughter's real file, erased by Meridian decades ago. Beat: everyone in this story is row twelve.

chapters.title: The Missing Founder
chapters.summary: Orsen and Nia POV, alternating. They find the third founder living hidden in Porto—a woman who faked her death and warns that burning the archive will also erase every genuine memory stored inside it, including some of Orsen's real ones. Beat: the cost is named.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Quiet interlude: Orsen and Nia spend a stolen day cataloguing which memories Orsen will refuse to lose. The beach morning turns out to be real after all—Meridian edited around it, not over it. Beat: tenderness; hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Geneva Arrivals
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The summit convenes; Voss's protocol passes committee stage unnoticed inside a safety annex. Nia infiltrates as delegation staff; Orsen enters as credentialed press using a forged identity Meridian itself taught them to build. Beat: the trap closes on both sides.

chapters.title: Voss and Orsen
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Voss corners Orsen privately, offers the restoration one final time—and reveals the crash was retaliation for Orsen's father, a founder who tried to burn Meridian first. Orsen's grief has an inheritance. Beat: rage transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Annex 9
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. During the plenary vote, Nia hijacks the presentation feed and broadcasts fragments of the training archive—installed memories, manufactured investigators—to the delegates. Chaos; security converges. Beat: exposure as weapon.

chapters.title: The Burn
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In the server vault beneath the conference center, Orsen executes the burn sequence requiring their voiceprint, their father's key, and the founder's confession. To complete it, Orsen must purge the archive copy containing their daughter's real file. Beat: climax—sacrifice as authorship of self.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. The summit collapses the annex; Voss is arrested by his own board's contingency protocol. Nia finds Orsen on the lake shore, hollowed but present. Neither reports the other. Beat: exhaustion, and the first honest silence between them.

chapters.title: Row Thirteen
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Weeks later, Orsen takes a low-level safety job far from aviation's center, flying economy, sitting deliberately in row thirteen. They keep one unedited photo of their daughter and let the rest go. Beat: mourning without architecture.

chapters.title: The Protocol of Kowloon
chapters.summary: Dual epilogue POV. In Kowloon, a residual Meridian node pings once, unanswered. Nia arrives at Orsen's door with no handler, no file, just a question about dinner. Orsen answers the door without checking the peephole. Beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.
